speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction, such as how long it lasted and if it was difficult to stop? Also, do you have a family history of bleeding disorders or easy bruising?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the bleeding typically stop on its own after a few hours, or does it require medical intervention like transfusions or clotting factors? Have you ever experienced bleeding into your joints, particularly in the knees or elbows?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you personally experience bleeding into your joints, such as hemarthrosis, or is that limited to your family history? To help distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, I will request clotting factor assays. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_activity, Factor_IX_activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX are normal, we need to look at the extrinsic pathway. I will request a Prothrombin Time test to evaluate Factor VII activity. REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Prothrombin Time rules out a factor VII deficiency, so I need to assess the intrinsic pathway to distinguish between von Willebrand disease and Hemophilia. I will request a Partial Thromboplastin Time test to evaluate the intrinsic clotting factors. REQUEST TEST: Partial_Thromboplastin_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged Partial Thromboplastin Time suggests an intrinsic pathway defect, but since Factor VIII and IX are normal, I suspect von Willebrand disease. REQUEST TEST: vWF_antigen, vWF_activity

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal vWF levels and a prolonged PTT, we must consider platelet function defects or rare clotting factor deficiencies like Factor XI. Do you have a personal history of bleeding into your joints, or is that strictly limited to your uncle's history? I will also request a platelet function assay to evaluate for qualitative platelet disorders. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_function_assay

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prolonged PTT with normal Factor VIII, IX, vWF, and platelet function, I suspect Factor XI deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Factor_XI_activity

speaker: Doctor
text: With all standard coagulation factors and platelet function normal despite a prolonged PTT, I suspect the presence of an inhibitor, such as a lupus anticoagulant, which can cause a false prolongation of the PTT without clinical bleeding. I will request specific tests to confirm this. REQUEST TEST: Lupus_anticoagulant_screen, Mixing_study

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lupus anticoagulant screen: Positive; Mixing study: Failure to correct PTT

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive lupus anticoagulant screen and failure to correct the PTT in the mixing study confirm the presence of an inhibitor, likely a lupus anticoagulant. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lupus Anticoagulant
